rationale: The target is a Shootout 'random' kernel: a tiny program dominated by a tight, hot numeric loop, so runtime overhead is the binding constraint and cost dimensions dominate the weights. SUB and SPLIT are cheap arithmetic/control-flow transformations with near-zero correctness risk, so they are weighted toward SecurityGain/DiversityGain and should apply broadly. BCF and FLA inflate loop-body work severely in hot kernels, so their RuntimeCost and SizeCost weights are high to restrict them to cold outer functions; FLA additionally gets a high CorrectnessRisk weight because flattening a state-machine random-number generator loop with floating-point comparisons risks altering iteration semantics under optimization. IBR and ICALL add indirect-call/branch overhead on a call- and branch-dense kernel, so they are allowed at moderate strength only where features indicate low execution frequency. IGV is enabled moderately since it improves diversity at low cost in a program this small, but its CorrectnessRisk weight is kept nonzero to avoid disturbing the compact global state the kernel relies on.
